extracted.intended_audience: systematic review authors (especially Cochrane review authors) conducting risk-of-bias assessments for intervention reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing, presenting, and incorporating risk-of-bias judgements for study results and syntheses in systematic reviews of interventions (Cochrane-focused). Covers assessor processes, documentation, presentation, analytic strategies, and handling conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate independent risk-of-bias assessments (C53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (at least) two people working independently to apply the risk-of-bias tool to each result in each included study, and define in advance the process for resolving disagreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicating the risk-of-bias assessment reduces both the risk of making mistakes and the possibility that assessments are influenced by a single person’s biases. Define in advance how disagreements will be resolved (e.g. discussion then adjudication by another author). Review authors assessing risk of bias should have content or methodological expertise (or both).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define process for resolving disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Review teams should define in advance the process for resolving disagreements about risk-of-bias judgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: both assessors attempt to resolve disagreements via discussion, and if that fails, call on another author to adjudicate the final judgement. Explore and resolve reasons for disagreement rather than relying on agreement statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on agreement statistics (e.g. kappa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not recommend use of statistical measures of agreement (such as kappa statistics) to describe the extent to which assessments by multiple authors were the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is more important that reasons for any disagreement are explored and resolved; transparent recording and justification of judgements is preferred over reporting agreement coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Review authors assessing risk of bias should have either content or methodological expertise (or both), and an adequate understanding of the relevant methodological issues addressed by the risk-of-bias tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is evidence that intensive, standardized training may significantly improve reliability of assessments (da Costa et al 2017). To improve reliability consider piloting the tool on a sample of articles (three to six papers suggested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify judgements and provide 'Support for judgement' (C54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify judgements of risk of bias (high, low and some concerns) and provide this information in the risk-of-bias tables (as ‘Support for judgement’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing support for the judgement makes the process transparent. Information may include direct quotes from study reports and an explanation for why a method is flawed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record sources of information for each judgement (C55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect the source of information for each risk-of-bias judgement (e.g. quotation, summary of information from a trial report, correspondence with investigator, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where judgements are based on assumptions from information outside publicly available documents, this should be stated. Cochrane authors are expected to record the precise location within a document that informed each judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select which results to assess for risk of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Review authors should think carefully about which results to assess for risk of bias, and assess risk of bias in results for outcomes that are included in the 'Summary of findings' table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary of findings tables typically include seven or fewer patient-important outcomes; guidance on constructing these is in Chapter 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation: full risk-of-bias tables (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full risk-of-bias table includes responses to each signalling question within each domain and risk-of-bias judgements, along with text to support each judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full tables are lengthy and generally should not be included in the main body of the review but should be made available for reference (e.g. supplementary material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation: forest plots showing RoB judgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use forest plots that present risk-of-bias judgements alongside the results of each study included in a meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a visual impression of the relative contributions of studies at different levels of risk of bias, especially when considered with study weights. Optionally, order or stratify plots by domain judgements or overall risk-of-bias judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation: bar graphs of contributions by risk category
rubrics_metrics.description: Review authors may generate bar graphs illustrating the relative contributions of studies with each risk-of-bias judgement (low, some concerns, high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dividing a bar into three regions, determine regions according to statistical information (e.g. precision, or weight in a meta-analysis) rather than by the number of studies in each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize risk of bias for each key outcome and study (C56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the risk of bias for each key outcome for each study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinforces the link between study design characteristics and possible impacts on study results and is a prerequisite for GRADE assessments of the certainty of the body of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address risk of bias in syntheses (C57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address risk of bias in the synthesis (whether quantitative or non-quantitative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: present analyses stratified according to summary risk of bias, or restrict analyses to studies at low risk of bias. Consider how study biases affect results when determining strength of conclusions and designs of future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use RoB 2 as primary tool when multiple tools used (C58)
rubrics_metrics.description: If randomized trials have been assessed using one or more tools in addition to the RoB 2 tool, use the RoB 2 tool as the primary assessment of bias for interpreting results, choosing the primary analysis, and drawing conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RoB 2 should take precedence for randomized trials to ensure consistency across Cochrane reviews and because it feeds directly into GRADE assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose strategy to incorporate bias into analysis and report in protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: When risks of bias vary across studies, choose an analytic strategy to incorporate assessments into analysis and describe the intended strategy in the review protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice affects which result is presented as the main finding. Consider trade-off between bias and precision; describe planned approach (restricted primary analysis, stratified analyses, presenting all + narrative, or bias-adjusted estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy 1: primary analysis restricted to low-risk studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict the primary analysis to studies judged to be at low risk of bias overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors restricting primary analysis this way are encouraged to perform sensitivity analyses to show how conclusions might change if high-risk studies were included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy 2: present multiple (stratified) analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Stratify analyses according to overall risk of bias to produce multiple estimates (e.g. all studies, low-risk-only, high-risk-only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include subgroup analyses by specific bias domains. Formal comparisons can use subgroup tests or meta-regression, but be cautious about low power; presenting multiple estimates may be confusing for decision-makers who require a single estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy 3: present all studies with narrative discussion (discouraged when risks vary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present an estimated effect based on all available studies plus description of risk of bias in individual domains or summary risk across studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discouraged when studies differ in risk of bias because such an approach can lead to conclusions that ignore bias and to overly precise pooled estimates. If used, incorporate summary risk-of-bias into measures of certainty (e.g. GRADE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy 4: adjust effect estimates for bias (bias adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust study results to attempt to remove bias, usually within a Bayesian framework with priors for bias size and uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be used as a sensitivity analysis but is not encouraged for Cochrane reviews because required assumptions are strong, expertise limited, and applicability issues exist across diverse audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting studies by risk of bias (caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies at high risk of bias should be given reduced weight in meta-analyses compared with low-risk studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological approaches for weighting by risk of bias are not sufficiently developed to recommend for Cochrane reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB tools focus on selection of the reported result; handle non-reporting at synthesis level
rubrics_metrics.description: RoB 2 and ROBINS-I focus on risk of bias for specific trial results, particularly whether a specific reported result was selected from multiple possible results on the basis of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective non-reporting and selective under-reporting of data (omitted or inadequately reported results) are not covered by RoB 2/ROBINS-I and should be assessed at the synthesis level as potential bias due to missing results (see Chapter 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider impact of dominance of high-risk studies on certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: When a meta-analysis is dominated by study results at high risk of bias, the certainty of the body of evidence may be rated lower than if such studies were excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider courses of action (restrict, stratify, adjust) and reflect the impact on GRADE assessments (Chapter 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add conflicts of interest directly to the RoB tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourage inclusion of conflicts of interest directly in the risk-of-bias assessment tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding conflicts of interest to the bias tool is inconsistent with its domain-based structure, and restricting consideration to an individual trial's bias overlooks impacts on trial design and on bias in a synthesis due to missing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and report funding and conflicts of interest information
rubrics_metrics.description: Review authors should describe funding information and conflicts of interest of authors for all studies in the 'Characteristics of included studies' table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide source information and consider exploring (e.g. subgroup analysis) whether trials with conflicts of interest have different or more variable effect estimates. Report a judgement (e.g. 'notable concern' vs 'no notable concern') and rationale in a table (trial identifier; judgement; rationale subdivided by who had conflicts and stages involved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical approach to identifying conflicts: rely on declared info, search extra sources when suspect
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing conflicts of interest, rely largely on declared conflicts but consider searching other sources (protocols, clinical study reports, Open Payments, ClinicalTrials.gov, other publications) when there is reason to suspect important conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance workload with expected gain. Rule of thumb: if unclear funding and no declaration from lead/corresponding authors, search Open Payments/ClinicalTrials.gov/other declarations. If no commercial funding and no declared conflicts, do not search additional sources. When lead/corresponding authors have clear conflicts, additional co-author searches may add little.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgement of 'notable concern' about conflict of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for a pragmatic judgement about whether there is reason for 'notable concern' about conflicts of interest affecting design, conduct, analysis, reporting, or synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider degree of conflicts and extent of involvement. A hypothetical undeclared conflict is usually insufficient. Examples: 'notable concern' for trials initiated/designed/analysed/reported by company employees; less concern for trials where company only supplied free medication and academics conducted the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on how conflicts of interest inform risk-of-bias judgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Review authors should explain how consideration of conflicts of interest informed their risk-of-bias judgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If analysis plans are lacking and investigators have important financial conflicts, judge selection of reported result as high risk. Conversely, do not up-rate risk-of-bias domains simply because investigators have conflicts if methods minimise bias. Optionally reflect on direction of bias (e.g. bias in favour of the experimental intervention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore conflicts of interest as potential source of heterogeneity and indirectness
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest may impact design choices (participants, comparator, outcomes) and thus affect directness and heterogeneity of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider conflicts when assessing indirectness and inconsistency in GRADE-related judgments and when interpreting heterogeneity in meta-analyses.
